name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+22 district fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent
Griffith holds roughly a 25-to-1 fundraising and cash advantage
Prediction markets price Democrats at about 3 percent
No public polls or expert ratings signal any competitiveness
model.rationale: Southwest Virginia's R+22 lean, Morgan Griffith's million-dollar war chest against Joy Powers' roughly $85,000 raised, and markets pricing his re-election near certain leave Powers without a visible path, even with a national environment tilted toward Democrats.
model.watch: Only a major wave of outside spending against Griffith or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would warrant rethinking this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan Griffith enters this Southwest Virginia contest as a heavy favorite. The district's partisan lean sits at R+22, Griffith has been renominated with more than $1 million in the bank, while Democrat Joy Powers has raised about $85,000 and holds under $15,000 on hand. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert race raters have flagged the seat as competitive.

Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 3 percent chance, and the favorable national environment would need to rival a historic wave to threaten a seat this red. The expected margin therefore sits near 19 points Republican, with uncertainty kept wide by the absence of polling. Absent extraordinary outside intervention, Griffith's path to another term is clear.
